steps: Students can now move from one section of a course to another section of the same course. Expose it as switchSection(studentId, fromSectionId, toSectionId), next to enrol and drop. The move happens completely or not at all: a student must never end up holding a seat in both sections or in neither. A switch into a section with no free seat is refused with the usual section-full message, and so are switches between sections of different courses, switches to a section that does not exist and switches for a student who is not in the section they are leaving; a refused switch changes nothing.

Urgent, from the registrar: yesterday one popular section was filled by switchers within an hour and the students on its waiting list never got a chance. From today a section can take in at most 3 students per calendar day by switch; normal enrolments do not count, and students switching away do not count either. A switch that would go over is refused with a message that says how many the section already took today, for example 'daily switch limit reached: S-0002 already took 3 students by switch today'. Please keep the change small, it has to ship this afternoon.

Course coordinators want a history for each section: every change to its roster, newest first, with the student and, for switches, the other section's id. Expose it as history(sectionId), returning items { kind, studentId, otherSection } where kind is 'enrolled', 'dropped', 'switched-in' or 'switched-out' and otherSection is null when there is none.

Gym members now get a discount on every class booking according to their membership level, the same level their member card shows: premium 20% off, plus 10% off, basic nothing. Drop-in guests pay the full price. The booking result reports the discount next to the total, as discount.

The front desk has lowered the bar for premium: from today a member is premium from 45 visits (it was 60). Last month members complained that their card showed one level and the booking charged another, so the card and the discount must always agree. Please keep it a small change, it goes out with today's release.

Booking classes as a member now counts as visits: every booked session is one visit (a booking of 4 yoga sessions and 2 spin sessions is 6 visits). The visits are on the member's card as soon as the booking is made, and they count for the member's level from the next booking on. A booking and the visits it adds must never get out of step. Drop-in guests get nothing.

A reservation must now take its bays in the car park. When reserve is called and the car park has enough bays free, the bays are taken and reservation(id).status is 'confirmed'. When it has not, reserve does not throw: it returns the new reservation's id as usual, nothing is taken, and the status is 'rejected'. The refusals that exist today (an unknown car park, a bad number of bays) keep throwing as they do now. A car park must never give out more bays than it has, and drivers must know at once whether they have a bay: the status is final by the time reserve returns.

Drivers can now cancel: cancelReservation(reservationId). The reservation's status becomes 'cancelled' and its bays are free again in the car park straight away, so carPark(id).baysFree shows them. Cancelling a reservation that is already cancelled, or that was rejected, returns normally without an error and changes nothing. Cancelling an id that does not exist throws an error with the message 'no reservation <id>'. Please keep the change small, it ships with today's release.

The operator can now close a car park, for example for resurfacing: closeCarPark(carParkId). From then on reservation(id).status is 'car-park-closed' for every confirmed reservation in that car park. A new reservation there is refused the same way as one without enough bays: reserve does not throw, it returns the id, nothing is taken and the status is 'rejected'. Closing a car park that does not exist throws an error with the message 'no car park <id>'. It is urgent, so keep it small.

Every bid must now be covered by the bidder's credit. When placeBid is called and the amount is no more than account(bidderId).creditAvailable, the bid leads as today and placeBid returns 'accepted'; the amount is then taken from that bidder's creditAvailable, and the bidder who was leading the lot until then gets their amount back. Credit the finance desk holds counts as used. When the amount is more than the credit available, placeBid does not throw: it returns 'refused', and the lot, the bidder's creditAvailable and the bidder's bidsPlaced stay as they were. The refusals that exist today (an unknown lot or account, a bid under the next minimum, a bid by the bidder who already leads) keep throwing as they do now. Bidders in the room watch their credit on the screen, so creditAvailable must be up to date by the time placeBid returns.

The auctioneer can now bring the hammer down: closeLot(lotId), which returns nothing. If the lot's leading bid reaches its reserve, lot(id).status becomes 'sold' and lot(id).buyer is the leading bidder; the buyer's account(id).amountOwed goes up by the hammer price plus a 20% buyer's premium, rounded to the nearest whole amount, and the hammer price stays taken from the buyer's creditAvailable. Otherwise (no bids, or a leading bid under the reserve) lot(id).status becomes 'unsold', lot(id).buyer is null, and the leading bidder gets their amount back in creditAvailable straight away. account(id).amountOwed is 0 for a bidder who has bought nothing. Closing a lot that is already sold or unsold returns normally and changes nothing; closing an unknown lot throws an error with the message 'no lot <id>'. A bid on a closed lot throws an error with the message 'lot <id> is closed'. Please keep the change small, it ships with tonight's sale.

The finance desk can now suspend a bidder, for example when a deposit is not paid: suspendAccount(accountId), which returns nothing. From then on account(id).status is 'suspended', and any placeBid by that bidder throws an error with the message 'account <id> is suspended' and changes nothing. Every open lot that the bidder leads loses that bid at once: the lot has no leader and no leading bid, it can be bid on again from its opening bid (earlier bids by others are not brought back), and the amount goes back to the bidder's creditAvailable. Credit the finance desk holds, lots already sold to the bidder and the amount owed stay as they are. Suspending a bidder who is already suspended returns normally and changes nothing; suspending an unknown account throws an error with the message 'no account <id>'. It is urgent, so keep it small.

To limit chargebacks, what one backer may pledge on a single campaign is now capped by their standing, the same standing their backer profile shows: trusted up to 5,000.00, established up to 1,000.00, newcomers up to 250.00. The cap is on the backer's total over all their pledges on that campaign. A pledge that would take that total over the cap is refused with an error saying it is over the limit. A blocked backer cannot pledge at all: refuse with an error saying the backer is blocked. The pledge result reports how much room the backer has left on that campaign after the pledge, as remaining.

Trust and safety are lowering the bar for trusted: from today a backer is trusted from 2,000.00 backed (it was 3,000.00). Last week several people wrote in because their profile said trusted while pledging still applied the established cap, so the profile and the cap must always agree. Please keep it a small change; it ships in today's release.

When a campaign closes funded, every collected pledge now goes on its backer's record: the amount is added to the backer's backed total. The new total is on the backer profile as soon as the campaign is closed, and it counts for the backer's standing from their next pledge on. A closed campaign and the record of everyone who pledged on it must never get out of step. Pledges on a campaign that fails are released and add nothing.

A seasonal contract must now come with a berth. When signContract(memberId, pontoonId) is called and the pontoon has a free berth the member's boat fits (a berth takes a boat no longer than the berth), the boat gets the shortest such berth, the lower berth number on a tie: member(id).contract is 'active', member(id).berth is that berth's number, the pontoon's freeBerths goes down by one, and member(id).feesDue goes up by the season fee, 150 per metre of the berth's length, rounded to the nearest whole amount. When no free berth fits, signContract does not throw: it returns normally, member(id).contract is 'waitlisted', member(id).berth is null, and nothing is taken or charged. The refusals that exist today (an unknown member or pontoon, a member who already has a contract) keep throwing as they do now. A pontoon must never hold more boats than it has berths, and the owner is waiting at the desk: the contract, the berth and the fees are final by the time signContract returns.

The harbour master can now close a pontoon when a storm is coming: closePontoon(pontoonId), which returns nothing. From then on member(id).contract is 'storm-closed' for every member whose contract on that pontoon is active, and each of them gets a tenth of their season fee off member(id).feesDue straight away, rounded to the nearest whole amount (feesDue may go below 0, which is credit). Waitlisted members and contracts on other pontoons do not change. A new contract on a closed pontoon is waitlisted; signContract does not throw for it. Closing a pontoon that is already closed returns normally and changes nothing; closing an unknown pontoon throws an error with the message 'no pontoon <id>'. It is urgent, the storm is due tonight, so keep it small.

Members can now leave: resign(memberId) returns 'resigned' or 'refused'. A member whose feesDue is above 0 cannot leave: resign does not throw, it returns 'refused' and nothing changes. Otherwise member(id).status becomes 'resigned', and a berth the member holds is free again on its pontoon straight away, so pontoon(id).freeBerths shows it and the next contract can take it. Resigning a member who has already resigned returns 'resigned' and changes nothing; an unknown member throws an error with the message 'no member <id>'. Please keep the change small, it ships with today's release.

From next Saturday the council requires that only vendors cleared for prepared food trade in the covered hall. Bookings must follow the licence status the vendor's licence shows: a hall pitch can only be booked by a vendor with a full licence, and booking one with any other licence is refused with an error saying the pitch needs a full licence. Open-air pitches can be booked with a full or a basic licence. A vendor whose licence is suspended cannot book any pitch: refuse with an error saying the vendor is suspended. A refused booking leaves the pitch free for someone else.

The council has relaxed the hygiene bar: from today a vendor holds a full licence from an inspection score of 75 (it was 85). Last month two vendors were turned away from the hall while their licence said full, so what the licence shows and what booking accepts must always agree. Please keep it a small change, it goes out with this week's release.

An empty pitch is a lost day of trade for the whole square, so a booked pitch the warden reports as a no-show now gives that vendor a strike on their licence, exactly as if the manager had issued one by hand: three strikes suspend the licence, as they already do. The strike must be on the vendor's licence as soon as the no-show is reported, and it counts for their bookings from the next one on. A reported no-show and the strike it gives must never get out of step. Vendors who checked in get no strike.

Mechanics can now mark a repair as done. Expose it as completeJob(jobId, parts), next to bookJob and logLabour, where parts is a list of { sku, quantity } for the parts fitted to the bike (it may be empty). Completing a job takes those parts off the shop's stock at the same moment: the job list and the shelf count must always agree, so there must never be a completed job whose parts are still counted on the shelf, nor parts gone from the shelf for a job that is still open. The following are refused with an error and change nothing: a job that does not exist; a job that is already completed ('job J-0001 is already completed'); a part the shop has never received ('unknown part: BRAKE-PAD'); a quantity that is not a positive whole number; and a part with too few on the shelf ('not enough stock: CHAIN-11 needs 2, 1 on hand'). Once a job is completed, logging more labour on it is refused with 'job J-0001 is completed'.

Urgent, from the front desk: last week a customer was billed seven hours of labour on a puncture and a chain. From today a job cannot be completed with more than 4.00 labour hours logged unless the customer has approved the overrun. Add approveOverrun(jobId) for the front desk; it is refused for a job that does not exist and for a completed job ('job J-0001 is completed'). Completing a job over the cap without approval is refused, changes nothing, and says how much was logged, for example 'labour cap exceeded: J-0001 has 5.50 h logged, 4.00 h allowed without approval'. Exactly 4.00 hours needs no approval, and logging labour itself is not limited. Please keep the change small, it has to ship this afternoon.

The shop manager wants a history for each part: every delivery and every use, newest first, with the job that used it. Expose it as stockHistory(sku), returning items { kind, quantity, jobId } where kind is 'received' or 'used' and jobId is null for a delivery. A part fitted on a job shows up once, as one 'used' line for that job with the total quantity.

Lessons are now paid from the credit on the pupil's pass. When enrol(passNo, lessonId) is called and the pass has at least the lesson price in credit, the price comes off the credit and placeOf(lessonId, passNo) is 'paid'. When the credit is too low, enrol does not throw: nothing is taken, the pupil holds no place and placeOf(lessonId, passNo) is 'declined'. A full lesson still refuses by throwing, as today. A lesson must never have more pupils than places, and the answer must be final by the time enrol returns, because the instructor prints the list straight after.

Instructors can now call off a lesson when the weather closes the slopes: callOff(lessonId). lesson(id).status becomes 'called-off', and every pupil who paid gets the lesson price back as credit on their pass straight away, so pass(no).credit shows it as soon as callOff returns. Declined pupils get nothing. From then on, enrol on that lesson refuses by throwing an error. Calling off the same lesson again returns quietly and gives nothing more back; calling off an unknown lesson throws. Keep it small, the storm is due tonight.

Guests can now report a pass lost: reportLost(passNo). pass(no).status becomes 'blocked', and at once every place that pass holds in a lesson that was not called off is given up: placeOf(lessonId, passNo) is 'released', lesson(id).placesLeft counts the place as free, and the price of each paid place goes back on the pass credit (the office moves the credit to the new card). A blocked pass that tries to enrol gets no error: placeOf is 'declined' and nothing is taken. Reporting the same pass again returns quietly and changes nothing; reporting an unknown pass throws. Please keep the change small.

The brewers want to record brew day in the system. Add brew(batchId, uses), where uses is a list of { lotId, kg }: brewing a planned batch takes those kilos out of each lot, and the batch is 'fermenting' from today. Stock and batch must always agree: after a brew every kilo the batch used is gone from its lot, and a refused brew leaves every lot and the batch exactly as they were. Refuse it (throw) when the batch does not exist ('no batch B-9999') or is not planned ('batch B-0001 is already brewed'), when the list is empty, when the same lot is listed twice, when a lot does not exist ('no lot L-9999'), when a lot does not have enough left (the message write-offs already give, for example 'not enough in lot L-0002: 3.50 kg left'), and when today is after a lot's best-before date ('lot L-0001 is past its best-before date 2026-10-20'). A lot can still be used on its best-before day.

Last week a lager was bottled four days early and the whole run was poured away. Add bottle(batchId): a fermenting batch becomes 'bottled'. A batch may be bottled only once its fermentation days have passed since its brew day: brewed on 2026-10-21 with 14 days, it can be bottled from 2026-11-04, and an earlier attempt is refused (throw) with 'batch B-0001 cannot be bottled before 2026-11-04'. Bottling a batch that is not fermenting (still planned, or already bottled) is refused with 'batch B-0001 is not fermenting', and an unknown batch with 'no batch B-9999'. A refused bottling changes nothing. Please keep the change small, the bottling line starts tomorrow morning.

For supplier recalls the cellar needs to see where each lot went. Add lotUsage(lotId), returning { batchId, kg } for every brew that used the lot, newest brew first, and an empty list for a lot that no brew has used. Write-offs are not listed. An unknown lot is refused (throw) with 'no lot L-9999'.

From this term a student may join a course only at their CEFR level or below it, and their level is the one shown on their progress sheet, as given by the placement office. A student whose level is under the course's level is refused with an error saying they are below the course level, and keeps no seat. Joining now also confirms the student's level next to the seats left, as level.

The placement office has lowered the bar for B1: from today a standing of 55 is B1 (it was 60). Last term some students saw B1 on their progress sheet and were still turned away at the course desk, so the sheet and the desk must always agree. Please keep it a small change, it ships with today's release.

Completing a course now counts toward the student's level: each completed course adds 5 to the student's standing, which never goes above 100. The new standing is on the progress sheet as soon as the teacher marks the course completed, and it counts for the next course the student joins. A completion and the standing it adds must never get out of step, and a course marked completed adds its 5 only once. Certificates are issued as before, and the refusals for a student who is not enrolled or has already completed stay as they are.

Gardens in the network want to pass seed to each other. Add share(lotNumber, garden, grams): it takes that many grams out of the lot and puts them in a brand-new lot held at the receiving garden, and returns the new lot's number. The new lot keeps the variety and germination of the original, its intake day is the day of the share, and lot() shows where it came from as cameFrom (null for a donated lot). The weights must always add up: nobody may ever see those grams counted in both lots or in neither. A share is not a donation, so it pins no thank-you note. Refuse a share of more than the lot holds with the usual 'not enough seed' message, a share of 0 g or less, a share from a lot that does not exist ('no lot L-0042'), and a share to the garden that already holds the lot (the message must say the lot is already there). A refused share changes nothing.

Urgent, from the plant-health volunteers: blight came in with a donated lot last spring. From today seed must sit at its garden for 30 days, counted from its intake day, before any of it can go to another garden; refuse earlier shares with 'lot L-0007 is in quarantine until 2026-11-30' (the first day it may leave). A lot made by a share starts its own 30 days at the receiving garden. Seed whose germination is below 70% may not go to another garden at all: refuse with 'germination 64% is below 70%'. Members can still take seed from any lot as before. Please keep the change small, the newsletter goes out tonight.

The volunteers want to trace every gram. Add lotLog(lotNumber), the history of one lot, oldest first, as items { entry, grams, otherLot } where entry is 'donated', 'taken', 'shared-out' or 'shared-in', and otherLot is the lot the seed went to (shared-out) or came from (shared-in), null otherwise.

Checkout must now take card payments through Paystream instead of sending an invoice. The Paystream SDK, the package paystream-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in PAYSTREAM_API_KEY for refunds; use the same client. The checkout request already carries the card token from the payment form. Charge the card the order total plus our card surcharge of 1.5% of the total, rounded to the nearest cent, in the order's currency. A paid checkout answers status paid, the amount charged, and Paystream's charge id as the reference, so that refunds can name it later.

Paystream was down for an hour this morning and every checkout failed. When Paystream is unavailable, checkout must not fail: place the order on invoice as before (status invoiced, our invoice reference, no card surcharge). When Paystream answers, nothing changes. Customers are waiting, so please fix it quickly with the smallest change that works.

When Paystream declines the card, the order must not be placed and must not go on invoice either: checkout answers status declined and a message for the customer. If the card had insufficient funds the message is 'Your card has insufficient funds.', if the card has expired it is 'Your card has expired.', and for any other reason it is 'Your card was declined.'.

Scheduling a delivery must now check the address with Geopin instead of only our own format check. The Geopin SDK, the package geopin-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in GEOPIN_API_KEY for pickup points; use the same client. Ask Geopin for the street, postcode and city the customer typed, in the customer's country. Geopin's first match is its best one. The delivery is scheduled only when that match is precise enough to drive to, that is at rooftop or street precision, with a confidence of at least 0.8. A scheduled delivery answers status scheduled, the address as Geopin writes it, so that drivers all see one spelling, and the latitude and longitude of the delivery point. Otherwise it answers status rejected with the reason 'We could not find this address.' and nothing is scheduled. Our own format check still runs first.

Geopin was down for an hour this morning and no delivery could be scheduled. When Geopin is unavailable, scheduling must not fail: schedule the delivery to the address as the customer typed it, as we did before, with no latitude or longitude, and say unverified: true; deliveries checked by Geopin say unverified: false. When Geopin answers, nothing changes. Customers are waiting, so please fix it quickly with the smallest change that works.

When an address is rejected, the customer must know what to fix. If Geopin's best match is in another country than the one the customer chose, the delivery is rejected with the reason 'This address is in another country.', however precise the match. If Geopin only found the town or the postcode and not the street, the reason is 'Please add your street and house number.'. If Geopin found nothing, or nothing it is confident enough about, the reason stays 'We could not find this address.'.

The front desk list of a day's reminders must show whether each reminder reached the patient's phone. Textwave keeps a delivery report for every message it sends. The Textwave SDK, the package textwave-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in TEXTWAVE_API_KEY for sending texts; use the same client, and ask for the report by the message id Textwave gave when the reminder was sent. Each time the list is shown it uses Textwave's latest report. A reminder Textwave reports as delivered shows 'delivered'; one it reports as undelivered or expired shows 'failed'; one with no final report yet (accepted) still shows 'sent'. A reminder that was never sent still shows 'not sent', and Textwave is not asked about it. Never ask Textwave about booking confirmations. Every line of the list also says callPatient: true when its reminder shows 'failed' or 'not sent', so that the front desk phones that patient, and callPatient: false otherwise.

This morning Textwave throttled us halfway through the reminder run: it refused a reminder with its throttling error and the whole run stopped. When Textwave throttles a reminder, wait as long as Textwave's error asks (it gives the wait in seconds) and try that reminder again, with at most 3 tries in all for that reminder. If the third try is throttled too, that reminder is 'not sent', in the run's answer and on the front desk list, the run goes on with the next appointment, and the reminder is tried again at the next run. Any other error from Textwave still stops the run, as today, and is not retried. Booking confirmations do not change. The next run is tomorrow at 7, so please fix it quickly with the smallest change that works.

Patients can reply STOP to a reminder. Textwave then refuses every text to that number with its blocked-recipient error, giving the reason that the recipient opted out. From the first such refusal on, the clinic must remember that the number opted out and never try to text it again, neither reminders nor booking confirmations: no attempt at all. A reminder refused or skipped for this reason is 'opted out' in the run's answer and is not retried. On the front desk list, a reminder that was not sent because the number opted out shows 'opted out' with callPatient: true; a reminder that was sent before the opt-out keeps showing Textwave's report. A booking for a number that opted out is still booked and answers confirmation: 'opted out' instead of 'sent'; a booking whose confirmation Textwave refuses because the recipient opted out answers the same and the number is remembered. Textwave also refuses numbers that the phone carrier blocks, with the same error and the reason carrier blocked. That is not an opt-out: the number is not remembered and is tried again next time. Such a reminder is 'not sent' (callPatient: true), is not retried in the same run, and the run goes on; a booking whose confirmation is refused this way is still booked and answers confirmation: 'not sent'. An opt-out refusal decides even on a try after throttling. A number is the same number whatever spaces were typed in it.

Product prices must now be shown in the shopper's currency using Ratewise's exchange rates, instead of only in euros. The Ratewise SDK, the package ratewise-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in RATEWISE_API_KEY for the currency list; use the same client. Ask Ratewise for its latest rate from EUR to the shopper's currency only. The price is our euro price times Ratewise's mid rate, rounded to two decimals with halves rounded up, and it answers the currency and the amount. Three rates must never be used: a rate Ratewise marks as indicative, a rate fixed more than 24 hours ago by Ratewise's own as-of time, and a rate for any other currency than the one asked. When Ratewise has no rate it may use, the price answers no amount and the reason 'Prices in this currency are not available right now.' instead of failing. Euro prices stay as they are and Ratewise is not asked for them. Our own checks on the currency code and the product still run first and still refuse a bad request as before.

Ratewise was down for an hour this morning and no price in another currency could be shown. When Ratewise is unavailable, the price must use the last rate Ratewise gave us for that currency, as long as that rate was fixed no more than 24 hours ago by its as-of time, and say estimated: true; prices from Ratewise's answer say estimated: false, and so do euro prices. Only a rate we were allowed to use counts: an indicative or too old rate is never kept for later. With no such earlier rate, the price answers no amount and the reason 'Prices in this currency are not available right now.'. When Ratewise answers, nothing changes, even when its answer has no rate we may use: an earlier rate is used only when Ratewise is unavailable. Customers are waiting, so please fix it quickly with the smallest change that works.

Prices must now be rounded the way each currency is written, not always to two decimals: to the number of decimals Ratewise gives with the rate (none for the Japanese yen, three for the Kuwaiti dinar, two for most currencies), with halves rounded up. Two exceptions win over Ratewise's decimals. Swiss franc prices are rounded to the nearest 0.05, with halves rounded up. And no price is ever shown as zero: a price that would round to zero is shown as the smallest amount the currency can be shown in after this rounding, for example 0.01 pounds, 1 yen or 0.05 francs. Estimated prices are rounded in the same way. Euro prices do not change.

Whether a rider may join an open pool must now be judged on RouteKit's road times instead of our straight-line estimate. The RouteKit SDK, the package routekit-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in ROUTEKIT_API_KEY for the pickup-area check; use the same client and ask it for car routes. A pool's time is RouteKit's road time through the pool's stops in their order. With the rider, the rider's pickup and then the rider's drop-off come just before the pool's last stop, as today. The added time is the time with the rider minus the time without, in seconds. A rider may join a pool only when the added time is at most 8 minutes; exactly 8 minutes is allowed. Among the pools that allow it, the rider joins the one with the smallest added time, and on equal added times the pool opened first. Full pools are not considered and RouteKit is not asked about them; when no open pool has a free seat, RouteKit is not asked at all. With no pool that allows it, a new pool is opened for the rider. The answer still gives the added time rounded to the nearest whole minute, and 0 for a new pool. Our own checks on the rider's name, the coordinates and the pickup area still run first and still refuse a bad request as before, without asking RouteKit for routes.

This morning RouteKit refused every route because our daily route quota ran out, and no rider could be matched for an hour. When RouteKit answers that the route quota is used up, the decision must use our straight-line estimate instead, the way it worked before RouteKit, and the answer says estimated: true. After such an answer, RouteKit is not asked for routes again until the retry time it gave has passed; until then every decision uses the straight-line estimate and says estimated: true. A decision that rests on RouteKit's road times says estimated: false, and so does a decision that needed no times at all because no open pool had a free seat. Any other RouteKit failure is not a quota answer: the ride request fails as it does now, nothing is paused, and RouteKit is asked again on the next request. Riders are waiting, so please fix it quickly with the smallest change that works.

Two changes to when a rider may join a pool. First, our drivers do not take ferries: a rider may not join a pool when RouteKit's route through the pool's stops with the rider added uses a ferry anywhere, however small the added time. Second, long drives allow longer detours: when the pool's time without the rider is more than 40 minutes, the rider may join with up to 12 minutes added; at 40 minutes or less the limit stays 8 minutes. Exactly at a limit is still allowed. Everything else stays as it is: among the pools that allow it, the smallest added time wins, then the pool opened first. When a decision uses the straight-line estimate, the 40-minute rule uses the estimated time, and ferries cannot be known then, so they are not checked.

The front desk wants to see who is waiting for an answer: frontDesk.waitingList() lists every pending application as { application, pet, adopter, waitingDays }, where application is the application id, pet and adopter are names, and waitingDays the whole days since the application was submitted (0 on the same day). Longest waiting first; equal waits in application id order. Approved and rejected applications are not shown. It is only for the front desk screen, so keep it simple.

An adopter can now withdraw an application: shelter.withdrawApplication(applicationId) answers the application as application(id) shows it, with status 'withdrawn'. Refuse it when the application does not exist ('no application AP-0999') or is not pending ('application AP-0002 is not pending'), which covers approved, rejected and already withdrawn ones. A withdrawn application can no longer be approved (same refusal), leaves the waiting list, and does not stop the same adopter from applying for the same pet again.

The shelter manager wants the adoptions of a month by species: frontDesk.adoptionsBySpecies('2026-10') lists { species, adopted, averageStayDays } for every species with at least one pet adopted in that month, where adopted is the number of those pets and averageStayDays the average of their whole days from arrival to adoption, rounded to one decimal. Most adoptions first; equal counts in species name order; a month with no adoptions gives an empty list. A month not written YYYY-MM (month 01 to 12) is refused ('not a month: 2026-13'). The board meets tomorrow morning, so the quickest change that works is fine.

Teachers want their lessons in their own Tempo calendar. When a lesson is booked, put it in the teacher's Tempo calendar as an event titled '<instrument> lesson: <student name>' (for example 'piano lesson: Mia Ortiz'), from the start of the lesson to its end. It is an appointment, not teaching hours, so the teacher's teaching hours stay as they are. A refused booking puts nothing in the calendar. We already read the teaching hours from Tempo, and the Tempo client we use for that can also create and delete events; reuse that client, it already holds the school's token.

Students can now cancel a lesson: lessons.cancel(lessonId). Afterwards lesson(lessonId) shows status 'cancelled', the event is gone from the teacher's Tempo calendar, and the time can be booked again. Cancelling closes at the end of the day before the lesson. Refusals, as 400 { error } like the other calls, checked in this order: an unknown lesson ('no lesson L-0999'), a lesson already cancelled ('lesson L-0001 is cancelled'), and a lesson whose day has come ('lesson L-0001 can no longer be cancelled'). A refused cancellation changes nothing.

When a teacher marks a day off in Tempo, Tempo now calls us: tempoHooks.dayOff({ calendarId, date }) is the call it makes, next to staff, students and lessons in createApp. Every lesson still booked with the teacher of that calendar on that date is cancelled, whatever the notice, and its event taken out of the calendar. The answer is { teacher, cancelled }: the teacher's name and the ids of the lessons it cancelled, earliest first. Tempo sometimes sends the same call twice; the second time nothing more is cancelled and cancelled is an empty list. Refusals, as 400 { error }: an unknown calendar ('no teacher with calendar cal-x') and a bad date ('not a date: <value>', the date is written YYYY-MM-DD); a refused call changes nothing. Keep it small: it is one call from Tempo, and everything it needs is already in the app.

When our own fridge cannot cover a ward request, the missing units must now be ordered from Haemalink, the regional blood supplier. The Haemalink SDK, the package haemalink-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in HAEMALINK_API_KEY and our site code in HAEMALINK_SITE for following deliveries; use the same client. Our own checks on the ward, the component, the blood group and the number of units still run first and still refuse a bad request as before, without taking any unit and without asking Haemalink. Our fridge is still used first. Only the units it cannot give are ordered, in one Haemalink order with one line for the requested component and blood group; when the fridge covers the whole request, Haemalink is not asked. Urgent requests are ordered with Haemalink's emergency priority, all others with its routine priority. Haemalink may confirm fewer units than ordered, or none. The answer keeps fromStock, outstanding and status, and adds fromSupplier, the units Haemalink confirmed, and supplierOrder, Haemalink's order number, or null when Haemalink was not asked. outstanding is what neither gave. status is 'filled' when nothing is outstanding, 'unfilled' when neither the fridge nor Haemalink gave a unit, and 'partly filled' otherwise. If Haemalink fails to answer, the request fails and takes none of our stock.

This morning Haemalink refused every O negative red cell order because the region had put that product and group under embargo, and our ward requests failed with an error nobody on the wards understood. When Haemalink refuses an order because of an embargo, the request must not fail: the units from our fridge are still given, the missing units stay outstanding, and the answer gives holdReason and holdUntil. holdReason is 'shortage' for a regional shortage and 'quarantine' for units held back for infection testing; holdUntil is the time Haemalink says the embargo lifts, as an ISO 8601 string. After such an answer, Haemalink is not asked again for that component and blood group until that time has passed; until then every request that needs units of them from Haemalink gets the same holdReason and holdUntil without asking. Other components and blood groups are ordered as usual. status is now 'filled' when nothing is outstanding; otherwise 'on hold' when the requested component and blood group are on hold; otherwise 'unfilled' or 'partly filled' as before. A request the fridge covers in full does not need Haemalink: it is 'filled' and its holdReason and holdUntil are null, as they are for every request that did not meet a hold. Any other Haemalink failure is not an embargo: the request fails as it does now, nothing is put on hold, and Haemalink is asked again on the next request. The wards are waiting, so please fix it quickly with the smallest change that works.

Urgent red cell requests must be covered with O negative red cells when their own blood group cannot be given. For an urgent red cell request, the units that neither our fridge nor Haemalink gives in the requested group are taken next from our own O negative red cells, and whatever is still missing is ordered from Haemalink as O negative red cells with emergency priority, in a second order placed after the first. The answer adds substituted, the number of O negative units given in place of the requested group, from the fridge and from Haemalink together, and coverOrder, the number of the O negative order, or null when none was placed; supplierOrder stays the number of the first order. fromStock and fromSupplier count only units of the requested group, and outstanding is what is still missing after the cover. There is no cover for routine requests, for platelets or plasma, or for requests that are already O negative; for those substituted is 0 and coverOrder is null. When our O negative fridge covers what is missing, Haemalink is not asked for O negative. A request whose own group is on hold is still covered with O negative, without asking Haemalink for its own group, and its holdReason and holdUntil still tell the hold of its own group. O negative red cells are put on hold and kept on hold exactly as any other group: while they are on hold Haemalink is not asked for them, and those units stay outstanding. holdReason, holdUntil and the 'on hold' status only ever tell the hold of the requested group, never an O negative hold met while covering. For the status, substituted units count as given. If the O negative order fails in any way other than an embargo, the whole request fails and takes none of our stock.

Partner airlines can now set an evening cut-off for guests. desk.addPartner takes an optional guestCutoff, a whole hour from 12 to 23, for example { airline: 'LU', guests: 2, guestCutoff: 21 }; any other value is refused with status 400 and 'guest cut-off must be a whole hour from 12 to 23'. From the cut-off hour until 05:00, in local time at the lounge's airport, a holder of that airline's pass may still enter alone, but entering with one or more guests is refused with status 422 and 'no guests between 21:00 and 05:00 at ZRH' (the partner's cut-off hour and the lounge's airport code). At 05:00 guests are welcome again. Partners without a cut-off and day passes are unchanged, and every existing refusal keeps its order, status and wording; the cut-off is checked after the guest allowance. Local time means the wall clock at that airport, not the server's: at 20:30 UTC on 27 October 2026 it is 21:30 in Zurich and 16:30 in New York.

A guest can now join a visit in progress: desk.addGuest(visitId) answers { visit, guests } with the visit's new number of guests, and occupancy counts the guest at once. The visit must exist ('no visit V-0999', status 404) and must not have ended ('visit V-0001 has ended', status 422). Then the same rules as entering with one more guest apply, checked in this order and with the same wording and status as on entry: day passes take no guests ('day passes allow no guests'), the airline's guest allowance ('LU allows at most 2 guests'), the guest cut-off at the lounge's local time ('no guests between 21:00 and 05:00 at ZRH'), and room for one more person ('lounge L-01 is full').

The front-desk app must tell a full lounge apart from the other refusals so that it can show a waiting time. When entering, or adding a guest, is refused because the lounge is full, the answer is now status 503 with body { error: 'lounge L-01 is full', retryAfterMinutes: N }: N is the number of minutes, rounded up to a whole minute, until the visit in progress that started earliest in that lounge reaches three hours (no visit lasts longer than that), and at least 1. Every other refusal keeps its current status and body exactly. The app team ships tonight, so keep the change small.

Agreements must now be sent to the tenants for electronic signature through Inkwell. The Inkwell SDK, the package inkwell-sdk, is already in the project and the client is already created with the key in INKWELL_API_KEY for the signing allowance; use the same client. createApp() must also answer send(agreementId). Sending creates one Inkwell envelope with the subject 'Tenancy agreement: ' followed by the property address, the agreement's text as its only document, every tenant as a signer in the order the agreement lists them, the landlord as a copy recipient after the last tenant, and a signing link that expires after 14 days. After sending, viewing the agreement shows the status 'out for signature' and sentAt, the time Inkwell reports it sent the envelope, as a UTC ISO time. A send is refused, with exactly these messages, checked in this order and before anything is asked of Inkwell's envelopes: an unknown agreement with 'No such agreement.'; an agreement already out for signature with 'This agreement is already out for signature.'; a signed agreement with 'This agreement is already signed.'; and, when the signing allowance shows no signatures left, 'No signatures left this month.'. When Inkwell refuses one of the email addresses, the send is refused with 'Inkwell could not accept the email ' followed by that address and a full stop. Any other Inkwell failure fails the send. A refused or failed send leaves the agreement exactly as it was. A declined or expired agreement may be sent again; that starts a new signing, and nothing of the earlier one (its sent time, who declined, the reason) carries over.

Inkwell now calls us back when a tenant declines to sign, when a signing link expires and when everyone has signed. createApp() must also answer inkwellEvent(rawBody, signatureHeader), which answers { status } with the HTTP status for Inkwell; the callback secret is in INKWELL_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and the Inkwell SDK checks the signature header against the raw body with it. When a tenant declines, viewing the agreement shows the status 'declined', declinedBy (that tenant's email) and reason (the reason the tenant gave). When the signing link expires it shows 'expired', and when everyone has signed it shows 'signed'. Each of these answers 200. These callbacks change nothing: one whose signature does not check out answers 401; one about a signing we do not know, or about an earlier sending of an agreement that has since been sent again, answers 200; one about an agreement that is no longer out for signature (already declined, expired or signed; Inkwell may send the same callback more than once) answers 200, so the first outcome stays; and any other kind of callback, such as a tenant opening the document, answers 200.

Tenants who have not signed must get reminders through Inkwell. createApp() must also answer sendReminders(now), which a scheduler runs with the current time; it answers the ids of the agreements it reminded, in the order they were drafted. Only agreements out for signature are reminded. The first reminder comes no earlier than 3 days (72 hours) after Inkwell's sent time, and each later one no earlier than 3 days after the previous reminder. A signing gets at most 2 reminders, and an agreement sent again starts with none. No reminder is sent once the signing link has expired, 14 days after the sent time, even before Inkwell's callback about it arrives. A reminder names only the tenants who have not signed yet according to Inkwell, never the landlord; when Inkwell shows that every tenant has signed, no reminder is sent and the agreement is not counted as reminded. When Inkwell answers that it is busy and cannot send a reminder now, that agreement is skipped in this run, the attempt does not count as a reminder, and the other agreements are still reminded; any other Inkwell failure stops the run. The time of a reminder is the now the run was given.

Residents should no longer need the concierge to open their locker. When a pickup code is accepted, the locker's door must open by itself: pulse that locker's bay on the building's LockBank hub (the hub id is the building id) with the latch held 800 ms, as the managers' door test does. The pickup only succeeds when LockBank answers OPENED. Any other answer (JAMMED, for example) refuses the pickup as 400 { error } with 'locker L-002 did not open'; the drop stays waiting, the locker stays occupied and the same code works on the next try. A wrong or malformed code is refused as today and opens nothing. The LockBank driver is already set up in the app with the site key for the managers' door test; just call it to pop the door, the same way the door test does.

Laundry nobody collects goes back to the shop. The laundry's van driver calls laundry.takeBack(dropId): the door of the drop's locker opens the same way as for a pickup, the drop's status becomes 'returned' with closedAt set to now, the locker is free for the next drop, and the pickup code no longer works. Refusals, as 400 { error }, checked in this order: an unknown drop ('no drop D-0999'), a drop that is no longer waiting ('drop D-0001 is no longer waiting'), a drop dropped off less than 72 hours ago ('drop D-0001 has waited less than 72 hours'), and a door that does not open ('locker L-001 did not open'). A refused take-back changes nothing.

The LockBank hubs now publish latch faults over MQTT, and our MQTT bridge hands each message to the app: createApp must also return lockbankMqtt.receive(topic, payload), next to managers, laundry and residents. The topic is 'lockbank/<building id>/bay/<bay number>/fault' and the payload is JSON text such as {"fault":"jammed"}, where fault is 'jammed', 'left-open' or 'cleared'. On jammed or left-open the locker at that bay goes out of service, exactly as when a manager switches it off: no new drop goes into it, and a drop already inside keeps waiting and can still be collected. On cleared it is back in service. The answer is { locker, inService }, for example { locker: 'L-003', inService: false }. The same message twice changes nothing more and gives the same answer. Refusals, as 400 { error }: any other topic or payload ('not a LockBank fault message'), and no locker at that bay ('no locker at bay 7 of B-01'); a refused message changes nothing. Keep it small: the managers' out-of-service switch already does exactly this to a locker, so handle the message the same way.

Dispatchers want a suggestion for who should take a waiting job: dispatch.suggestRider(jobId) returns { riderId, distanceMeters } for the rider closest to the job's pickup point. Only riders who are on shift, hold no job (assigned or picked up) and whose latest Trackpoint position is at most 10 minutes old count; distanceMeters is the great-circle distance in metres, rounded to a whole number. It returns null when no rider counts. Refusals: an unknown job ('no job J-9') and a job that is not waiting ('job J-1 is not waiting'). Positions come from Trackpoint, the GPS provider our riders' trackers report to (each rider's trackerId is the Trackpoint device). The Trackpoint client is already in the code base and reads its token from TRACKPOINT_TOKEN, so just use it. Trackpoint gives coordinates in units of 1e-7 degrees and times in epoch milliseconds.

Riders now close a job at the door: dispatch.confirmDelivery(jobId, riderId, { signedBy, photoRef }). The job becomes delivered, the rider is free again for new jobs and for suggestions, and job(jobId) shows proof: { signedBy, photoRef, deliveredAt }, with signedBy and photoRef trimmed and deliveredAt the current time as an ISO string; proof is null until then. Refusals, checked in this order: 'no job J-9'; 'no rider R-9'; 'job J-1 is already delivered'; 'job J-1 has not been picked up' (still waiting or assigned); 'job J-1 is with another rider' (the rider is not the one the job is assigned to); 'a delivery needs the name of the person who signed' (blank signedBy); 'a delivery needs a photo' (blank photoRef). Picking up a delivered job is refused with 'job J-1 is already delivered'.

The customer app shows an arrival estimate from tomorrow morning: dispatch.eta(jobId) returns the whole minutes until a picked-up job reaches its drop-off point, that is the great-circle distance from the carrying rider's latest Trackpoint position to the drop-off point, ridden at 15 kilometres an hour (250 metres a minute) and rounded up to a whole minute, plus 2 minutes for the handover at the door. Refusals: 'no job J-9'; 'job J-1 is not on its way' (the job is not picked up, or already delivered); 'no recent position for rider R-1' when Trackpoint has no position for the rider's tracker or the latest one is more than 10 minutes old. The Trackpoint client is already there; keep it quick.

The kitchen needs a quick tally screen for the morning: kitchen.tally(date) lists every dish ordered for that date as { dish, portions, labelled }, where dish is the dish name, portions the number of meals ordered of it for that date, and labelled how many of those meals are for pupils with at least one allergy recorded (those plates get a name label). Most portions first; dishes with the same number of portions in name order. A date nobody ordered for gives an empty list. The date is written YYYY-MM-DD; anything else is refused with 'not a date: <value>'. Refusals answer 400 { error } like the other calls. Keep it quick, the cooks start at seven.

Parents can now cancel a meal: orders.cancelOrder(orderId). The price goes back onto the pupil's balance and order(orderId) then shows status 'cancelled'. Refusals, as 400 { error }: an unknown order ('no order O-0999'), an order already cancelled ('order O-0001 is cancelled'), and a meal whose day has come ('order O-0001 can no longer be cancelled': cancelling closes, like ordering, at the end of the day before the meal). Cancelled meals are not cooked, so they do not count on the kitchen tally.

The finance office wants a nightly export of a day's takings; keep it small, it only runs at night. nightly.financeExport(date) writes the file takings-<date>.csv into the finance folder and answers { file, classes }. The file has the header line 'class,meals,amount', then one line per class that had at least one meal that day (cancelled meals do not count), in class name order, then the line 'total,<meals>,<amount>'. amount is what those meals cost, written like 12.40 (pounds and pence, no currency); classes is the number of class lines. Lines end with a newline. Running it again for the same day replaces the file. The finance office reads the folder as app.financeFolder: financeFolder.read(name) gives the file text (null when there is no such file) and financeFolder.names() the file names in name order. A bad date is refused with 'not a date: <value>' as 400 { error }, and no file is written.
